# Government & Politics

Topics in this knowledge base concerning the government, political institutions, and governance of China.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: category-index — maintained by build-structure; do not edit by hand -->
| Topic | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| [The Tributary System](tributary-system.md) | The hierarchical framework of ritual, diplomacy, and trade through which imperial China structured its relations with neighboring states from the Han to the nineteenth century; tributary rulers acknowledged the emperor's suzerainty through the kowtow and periodic missions in exchange for legitimacy and regulated trade. |
| [The Imperial Examination System](imperial-examination-system.md) | The competitive written civil-service examination that selected imperial China's officials from the Sui and Tang through its abolition in 1905; grounded in the Confucian classics and Zhu Xi's Neo-Confucian orthodoxy, it enabled social mobility, standardized administrative competence, and shaped the scholar-official ideal for over a millennium. |
| [The Communist Party of China](communist-party-china.md) | The founding and ruling political party of the People's Republic of China since 1949, governing through the Leninist principle of democratic centralism. |
| [Chinese Civil War](chinese-civil-war.md) | Armed struggle (1927–1949) between the Nationalist Kuomintang and the Communist Party of China; the Communist victory established the People's Republic in 1949 while the defeated Nationalists retreated to Taiwan. |
| [The National People's Congress](national-peoples-congress.md) | The PRC's constitutionally "highest organ of state power" and chief legislature, established in 1954; nominally supreme, it functions in practice as a ratifying body for decisions made by the Communist Party. |
| [The 1989 Tiananmen Square Pro-Democracy Movement](tiananmen-square-1989.md) | A student-led popular protest in Beijing (April–June 1989) demanding democratic reform, press freedom, and an end to corruption; the People's Liberation Army suppressed it by force on June 3–4, killing hundreds to thousands and setting the framework of prosperity-for-conformity that has governed Chinese politics since. |
| [The Standing Committee of the Politburo](standing-committee-politburo.md) | The Communist Party's innermost decision-making body of 5–9 senior officials; formally the embodiment of collective leadership since the Deng era, it has increasingly concentrated power under Xi Jinping. |
| [The Hukou System](hukou-system.md) | China's household-registration system, established in 1951 and formalized by the 1958 regulations; its binary urban-rural classification bound citizens to their birthplace, channeled resources from countryside to city during the planned economy, and—though eased by reform-era migration and gradual liberalization—still stratifies access to schooling, healthcare, and welfare. |
